newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler-Benz recalls S-class Mercedes for repair.
newsitem.headline: Daimler-Benz recalls S-class Mercedes for repair.

text.p: German car maker Daimler-Benz AG said Friday it was recalling 68,700 S-class Mercedes cars produced between June 1995 and December 1996 for free repairs after a defect was found in the front brakes.
Daimler said that the recall would affect 24,200 S-class limousines in the United States and Canada, 15,700 in Germany, 7,600 in Japan and 21,200 in other countries.
The company said quality checks had found that in eight cars with the brakes fully applied the front wheels had come into contact with the brake hose, posing the risk of damage to the braking system.
There had, however, been no accidents due to the fault.

"In none of the cars was there the risk of brake failure," the statement said, adding that a double circulation system would have ensured sufficient braking power even if there had been a leak in the brake hose.
The company said that the repair would be free, and that new S-class models had already been fixed to avoid the potential problem.
